CRP / ESR / WCC raised in flare (non-specific)
eGFR / creatinine (CKD; guides allopurinol dose)

medications.label: Flare prophylaxis when starting ULT (low-dose colchicine)

examination.label: Loss of lumbar lordosis / thoracic kyphosis

BASDAI / ASDAS-CRP disease activity (biologic eligibility)

examination.label: Reduced active shoulder range of motion

Temporal artery biopsy (ideally within 1-2 weeks of steroids): giant cells, granulomatous inflammation, skip lesions

presentation.label: Visual loss / painful eye movements (optic neuritis)

examination.label: Optic neuritis / RAPD, pale optic disc

risks.label: Vascular RFs: HTN, DM, lipids, smoking, AF

examination.label: Speech: dysarthria / expressive or receptive dysphasia

Echo (TTE / TOE): LV thrombus, vegetations, PFO / bubble study, low EF

risks.label: Triggers: sleep deprivation, alcohol, missed meds, flashing lights

examination.label: Postictal state: drowsiness, confusion, Todd's paresis
Cardiovascular exam: pulse, BP, murmur (exclude syncope)

MRI brain (epilepsy protocol): hippocampal sclerosis, cortical dysplasia, tumour, cavernoma, gliosis
ECG: long QT / arrhythmia to exclude convulsive syncope
Bloods at first seizure: glucose, Na, Ca, Mg, renal function, LFTs (provoked / metabolic cause)
Video-EEG telemetry: differentiates epileptic from functional (non-epileptic) events; localises focus
Drug levels (phenytoin, valproate, carbamazepine) if toxicity or breakthrough seizures

medications.label: Sodium valproate (avoid in people who could become pregnant)

presentation.label: Memory: recent vs remote, repetitive questioning

examination.label: Cognitive screen: MMSE / MoCA / ACE-III, clock drawing

investigations.label: Formal cognitive testing: ACE-III / RUDAS (CALD) / neuropsychology: domain pattern (amnestic vs frontal vs visuospatial)

investigations.label: EMG / nerve conduction: active denervation (fibrillations, fasciculations) + chronic reinnervation in >=3 regions; normal sensory NCS

examination.label: Facial weakness (snarl smile), weak eye closure
Bulbar weakness: nasal speech, dysphagia, chewing fatigue

investigations.label: Acetylcholine receptor antibodies (~85% generalised); if negative: MuSK, LRP4
Repetitive nerve stimulation: decrement >10% in CMAP; single-fibre EMG (most sensitive): increased jitter
